Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)  
- Assessment consistent with severe migraine headache: sudden onset, persistent severe headache (8/10), photophobia, visual symptoms (shooting lights), positive family history (mother with migraines), partial response to analgesics, absence of neurological deficits or systemic signs  
- Differential diagnoses include:  
  - Migraine headache (High likelihood): supported by symptoms, family history, and clinical picture  
  - Venous sinus thrombosis (Moderate likelihood): oral contraceptive use, persistent severe headache with positional worsening and visual disturbances; no neurological deficits yet, requires imaging and further assessment  
  - Idiopathic intracranial hypertension (Medium likelihood): young woman, on oral contraceptives, headache worsened by positional change, visual symptoms; no papilledema or classic signs noted yet  
  - Intracranial hemorrhage (Low likelihood): sudden severe onset but absence of neurological signs, fever, or declining consciousness reduces likelihood  
  - Medication-induced headache from oral contraceptive (Low likelihood): no headache increase reported since pill initiation  
- Conflict noted: none between transcript and DDx; DDx expands on possible causes consistent with clinical presentation and risk factors  

Management Plan  
- Book appointment for full neurological examination including fundoscopy and blood pressure measurement  
- Consider prescribing stronger analgesics plus paracetamol, to be taken with food  
- Advise patient to attend emergency care if headache worsens, neurological symptoms develop, or headache becomes unbearable before appointment  
- Discuss possible migraine diagnosis and pill review if migraine confirmed on examination; note possible need to change contraceptive pill if migraines progress with aura  
- Provide patient education about headache monitoring and precautions
